FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after 
the draft finalized by the Dye Intermediates Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 


2-Nitro-4-methoxyaniline is an intermediate for dyestuffs and pigments. It is also known as 
fast bordeaux (GP base) and C.I. azoic diazo component 1. The material is represented by the 
following formula: 


NH» 
NO; 


OCH3 


2-NITRO-4-METHOXYANILINE 
[MOLECULAR MASS: 168.15] 


(CAS REGISTRY NO.: 96-96-8) 


This standard was first published in 2002. The committee responsible for the preparation of 
this standard decided to revise it to incorporate recent developments in analytical techniques 
and use of more sophisticated instrument to determine purity and impurity profile. In this 
(first) revision, high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) method for determination 
of 2-nitro-4-methoxyaniline content (assay) has been incorporated. 


The composition of the committee responsible for formulation of this standard is listed in 
Annex D. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied 
with, the final value, observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be 
rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values 
(second revision)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should 
be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 15134 : 2023 


Indian Standard 
2-NITRO-4-METHOXYANILINE, TECHNICAL — 
SPECIFICATION 
( First Revision ) 
1 SCOPE IS No. Title 


This standard prescribes the requirements, 
the methods of sampling and testing for 
2-nitro-4-methoxyaniline. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed below contain 
provisions which, through reference in this 
text constitute provisions of this standard. 
At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision and parties to 
agreement based on this standard are 
encouraged to investigate the possibility of 
applying the most recent editions of the 
standards listed below: 


IS No. Title 
IS 1070 : Reagent grade water 
1992 


(third revision) 


IS 2552: Steel drums (galvanized and 
1989 ungalvanized) — Specification 
(third revision) 


IS 5299 : Methods of sampling and 


2001 tests for dye intermediates 
(first revision) 


3 REQUIREMENTS 
3.1 Description 


The material shall be in the form of dry 
reddish-brown powder and shall be free 
from visible impurities. 


3.2 The material shall also comply with 
the requirements given under Table 1, 
when tested according to the methods 
prescribed in col (4) and col (5) of Table 1.

D In case of disputes, determination of assay by HPLC, shall be the referee method. 


IS 15134 : 2023 


4 PACKING AND MARKING 
4.1 Packing 


The material shall be packed in suitable 
paper/plastic bags, plywood boxes or 
drums (conforming to IS 2552) or as 
agreed to between the purchaser and the 
supplier. 


4.2 Marking 


4.2.1 Each container shall be securely 
closed and shall bear legibly and indelibly 
the following information: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name of manufacturer and his 
recognized trade-mark, if any; 

c) Net mass of material; 

d) Month and year of the 
manufacture; 

e) Batch or lot number; and 

f) Any other statutory requirements. 


4.2.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the 
requirements of this standard may be 
certified as per the conformity assessment 
schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and 
the Rules and Regulations framed 
thereunder, and the products may be 
marked with the Standard Mark. 


5 SAMPLING 


5.1 The method of drawing representative 
samples of the material shall be as 
prescribed in 4 of IS 5299. 


5.2 Numbers of Tests 


5.2.1 Tests for description, melting point 
and assay shall be done on the individual 
samples. 


5.2.2 Tests for matter insoluble in diazo 
and moisture content shall be performed 
on the composite sample. 


5.3 Criteria for Conformity 
5.3.1 For Individual Samples 


The lot shall be declared as conforming to 
the requirements of the description, 
melting point and assay, if each of the 
individual test results satisfies the relevant 
requirements given at 3.1 and in Table 1. 


5.3.2 For Composite Sample 


For declaring the conformity of the lot to 
the requirements of matter insoluble in 
diazo and moisture content, while tested 
on the composite sample, the test result 
shall satisfy the relevant requirements 
given in Table 1. 


6 TEST METHODS 


6.1 Tests shall be conducted according to 
the methods prescribed and as referred in 
col (4) and col (5) of Table 1. 


6.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, ‘pure 
chemicals’ and distilled water (see 
IS 1070) shall be employed in tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do 
not contain impurities which affect the results of analysis. 


IS 15134 : 2023 


ANNEX A 
[Table 1, S1 No. (11)] 
DETERMINATION OF 2-NITRO-4-METHOXYANILINECONTENT (ASSAY) BY 
NITRITE VALUE 


A-1 APPARATUS 

A-1.1 Burette, 50 ml. 

A-1.2 Beaker, 1 000 ml. 

A-2 REAGENTS 

A-2.1 Concentrated Hydrochloric Acid 
A-2.2 Potassium Bromide 


A-2.3 Standard Sodium Nitrite Solution, 
0.5 N. 


A-2.4 Potassium Starch Iodide Paper 
A-3 PROCEDURE 


Weigh accurately 4.000 g of the sample 
into the beaker containing 100 ml glacial 
acetic acid, warm the beaker to dissolve 
the material completely. Add 50 ml 
concentrated hydrochloric acid. Cool to 


5 °C and then add 5 g of potassium 
bromide. Titrate with 0.5 N sodium nitrite 
solution to a distinct blue ring on starch 
potassium iodide paper. The end point 
should persist for 5 min without further 
addition of sodium nitrite solution. Preserve 
the solution for diazo insoluble. 


A-4 CALCULATION 


V x N x 16.815 


Assay, percent by mass = m 


where 


V = volume of sodium nitrite solution, 
ml; 

N = normality of sodium nitrite solution; 
and 

M = mass of sample taken for test, g. 


IS 15134 : 2023 


ANNEX B 
[Table 1, SI No. (ii)] 


DETERMINATION OF 2-NITRO-4-METHOXYANILINE CONTENT (ASSAY) BY 
HIGH PERFORMANCE LIQUID CHROMATOGRAPHY (HPLC) 


B-1 GENERAL 


High-performance liquid chromatography 
or high-pressure liquid chromatography 
(HPLC) is a chromatographic method that 
is used to separate a mixture of compounds 
in analytical chemistry and biochemistry to 
identify, quantify or purify the individual 
components of the mixture. 


B-2 APPARATUS 


B-2.1 Binary Gradient Liquid 
Chromatography System — with UV 
detector capable of being operated under 
conditions suitable for resolving the 
individual constituents into distinct peak 
may be used. 


B-2.2 COLUMN 


C18 column of 100 A with length 250 m, 
internal diameter 4.6 mm and particle size 
5 um or equivalent. 


B-3 REAGENTS 
B-3.1 Acetonitrile — HPLC grade. 
B-3.2 Water — HPLC grade. 


B-3.3 Sodium Dihydrogen 
Orthophosphate — HPLC grade. 


B-3.4 Tetra-n-butylammonium — HPLC 
grade. 


B-3.5 2-Nitro-4-methoxyaniline, Bromide 
— known purity. 


B-4 STANDARD PREPARATION 
Weigh accurately 0.050 0 g 2-nitro-4- 


methoxyaniline in 100 ml volumetric 
flask. Dissolve it in acetonitrile and 
make it up to the mark with acetonitrile. 


B-5 SAMPLE PREPARATION 


Weigh accurately 0.050 0 g sample in 
100 ml volumetric flask. Dissolve 
it in acetonitrile and make it up to the 
mark with acetonitrile. 


B-6 BUFFER PREPARATION 


Take 5.000 0 g tetra-n-butylammonium 
bromide and 1.666 6 g sodium dihydrogen 
orthophosphate in 1 1 volumetric flask. Add 
200 ml. HPLC grade water and completely 
dissolve it. Make total volume with HPLC 
grade water. 


B-7 FLOW RATE, 1.00 ml/min. 
B-8 MOBILE PHASE 


Acetonitrile Buffer 


30 ; 70 


B-9 COLUMN OVEN TEMPERATURE, 
40 °C. 

B-10 INJECTION VOLUME, 5 ul. 

B-11 RUN TIME, 20 min. 


B-12 WAVELENGTH, 230 nm. 


B-13 PEAK TIME, 
methoxyaniline : 8.44 min. 


2-Nitro-4-

Calculate the peak area of individual 
constituent pertaining to  2-nitro-4- 
methoxyaniline on the chromatogram of 
the material. The concentration of the 
constituent may be obtained on the basis of 
peak area on chromatogram obtained with 
known amount of pure 2-nitro-4- 
methoxyaniline.

ANNEX C 
[Table 1, SI No. (iv)] 
DETERMINATION OF MATTER INSOLUBLE IN DIAZO 


C-1 APPARATUS 


C-1.1 Sintered Glass Crucibles G4 
Grade — 50 ml. 


C-1.2 Desiccator 
C-2 PROCEDURE 


Filter the solution preserved in A-3 through a 
tared G4 sintered glass crucible keeping the 
temperature at 0 °C to 5 °C throughout the 
filtration. Wash with cold water till the 
filtrate is colourless. Dry the crucible at 
(100 + 5) °C to constant mass. 


C-3 CALCULATION 


Insoluble in diazo, percent by mass 
(W, — W,) x 100 
= M 
where 
Wo = mass of crucible with insoluble, 
8; 
Wı = mass of crucible, g; and 


M = mass of sample taken for test, g.

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
